```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(castSDM)
```

## Fit a small response

The central workflow compares two predictor groups under one fitted response.
This complete example supplies a GLM through the external-model adapter.
The random data illustrate the interface and carry no ecological evidence.

```{r model}
set.seed(42)
current <- data.frame(temperature = rnorm(120), land = runif(120))
data <- transform(current, presence = rbinom(120, 1, plogis(temperature-land)))
model <- glm(presence ~ temperature + land, data, family = binomial())
fit <- cast_as_fit(list(glm = model), current,
  function(model, newdata) predict(model, newdata, type = "response"))
future <- transform(current, temperature = temperature + .5, land = land + .1)
```

## Compare grouped scenarios

`cast_compare()` creates both partial scenarios without requiring separate
copies of environmental stacks. It freezes weights and records predictors
outside the groups as static.

```{r comparison}
comparison <- cast_compare(fit, current, future,
  groups = list(climate = "temperature", land_use = "land"), verbose = FALSE,
  thresholds = c(.3, .5, .7))
summary(comparison)[, c("component", "mean", "mean_supported", "n_valid")]
```

`climate_main` and `lulc_main` retain historical names for the first and second
groups. They are baseline simple effects. `climate_average` and `lulc_average`
average the effect over both levels of the other group. Interaction is joint
minus the two partial predictions plus current.

```{r plot, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
plot(comparison, las = 2)
```

These model-conditional contrasts do not identify real-world causal effects.
Presence/background predictions remain relative suitability unless an
appropriate calibration is established.

## Threshold sensitivity without new predictions

An external fit has no automatic evaluation score or threshold. For declared
threshold sensitivity, reuse the saved four-corner predictions:

```{r thresholds}
sensitivity <- summary(comparison, thresholds = c(.3, .5, .7))
sensitivity[sensitivity$component == "joint_change" & sensitivity$domain == "full", ]
```

The rule is `suitability >= threshold`. These summaries count rows or cells;
they are not area-weighted estimates. Supported counts use training marginal
quantiles, which cannot detect all novel environmental combinations.

## Built-in training workflow

For data with `lon`, `lat`, `presence` and numeric predictors, `cast_run()` uses
one protocol for screening, nested spatial CV, hold-out evaluation and refitting.
This small run uses grid blocks; design spatial validation for the actual study.

```{r training, eval=requireNamespace("ranger", quietly=TRUE) && requireNamespace("pROC", quietly=TRUE)}
species_data <- transform(data, lon = runif(120, 70, 130), lat = runif(120, 20, 50))
protocol <- cast_protocol(models = "rf", select_method = "full", rf_ntree = 30,
  cv_k = 2, block_method = "grid", aoa = FALSE, seed = 42)
run <- cast_run(species_data, protocol = protocol, verbose = FALSE)
summary(run)
run$diagnostics$holdout
run$diagnostics$folds
run$diagnostics$score_views_oof
comparison_run <- cast_compare(run, current, future,
  groups = list(climate = "temperature", land_use = "land"), verbose = FALSE)
comparison_run$threshold_source
```

Selection and tuning repeat inside CV folds. Independent hold-out data do not
choose weights. A usable pooled out-of-fold surface supplies the comparison
threshold; otherwise comparison returns continuous results only.

The automatic diagnostics include the frozen ensemble on the independent
hold-out, even without a prediction map. Training OOF native/shifted score
views preserve the same fitted engines and weights; they are descriptive,
not a new policy selected from hold-out labels. A weighted mean training-score
shift is not ecological probability calibration. Brier scores and reliability
bins concern the sampled response; background points are not known absences.
The protocol's clamp is used consistently in CV, evaluation and prediction;
AOA assesses original inputs. Historical results before 0.27.0 did not apply
the protocol clamp in CV or hold-out evaluation and should not be relabelled.

For aligned rasters, use the same call with `SpatRaster` objects, a mask and
`output_dir`. The advanced vignette demonstrates a small raster comparison.
